newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli arms merchant to Iran arrested in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Israeli arms merchant to Iran arrested in Israel.

text.p: An Israeli businessman, linked by foreign media reports to the alleged sale of chemical weapons parts to Iran in defiance of a U.S. embargo, has been arrested in Israel, his lawyer said on Wednesday.
Nahum Manbar, 51, has been in Israeli custody for the past three weeks but a court order banned the media from reporting his arrest. Israeli newspapers reported instead that he had gone missing.
A Tel Aviv magistrate's court partly lifted the gag order on Wednesday when it extended his detention by 10 days but prohibited disclosure of the suspicions against him.

Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Wednesday the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency recently gave the Jewish state information about Manbar's purported connections with Iran and asked it to take action.
"The judge said there are serious allegations against him. The court has limited what can be reported," Manbar's attorney Amnon Zichroni told Reuters.
He said Manbar has lived in France since 1985 and carried out most of his business activities outside of Israel. Manbar returned to Israel on March 27.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said U.S. President Bill Clinton sent a letter to Congress in 1995 accusing Manbar, along with two companies, of working to distribute forbidden material for the production of chemical weapons.
Foreign media reports said at the time he sold the material to Iran.
"Manbar denied it at the time and I suppose he still does," Zichroni said.
Asked in a 1995 interview in Haaretz whether he supplied Iran with Chinese-made material for the manufacture of poison gas, Manbar said: "Absolutely not."
But the newspaper quoted him as saying that he had supplied arms, including tanks, to Iran and had received Israeli Defence Ministry approval for what he exported.

"They (the Iranians) wanted me to build a chemical weapons plant in Iran. All these requests, which appeared suspect to me, I passed on to the proper authorities in Israel," he told Haaretz in the interview.

Israel, which has accused Islamic Iran of seeking its destruction, was a key middle man in the 1986-1987 Iran-Contra scandal in which White House aides secretly sold arms to Tehran and diverted profits to Nicaragua's contra rebels.
